title: Founding of the Kazakh Khanate
summary: The Kazakh Khanate arose around 1465 when the sultans Kerey and Janibek, who had left the Uzbek state of Abulkhair Khan, settled in the valley between the Chu and Talas rivers in Zhetysu. Kerey is named the first khan; he last appears in sources in the winter of 1473/74. Kazakhstan marked 550 years of the khanate in 2015.

uncertainty.note: The e-history.kz portal gives the formation as about 1465/66; Euronews gives 1465. Other pages put the earlier split from Abulkhair in the 1450s and the end year here only brackets the 1465/66 formation, not the khanate's later history.
